releases.title: Hear when a photo or calendar action goes through
releases.summary: Camera and Calendar now play distinct sounds when you take a photo, receive it in Gallery, schedule an event, or cancel it.
releases.body:
Open Camera and take a photo to hear a short tap when development starts. A second cue plays once the photo reaches Gallery for the active story. In Calendar, scheduling an event plays a confirmation and cancelling one plays a slide. All four effects work offline and use the existing sound toggle and notification volume.

Verification

Desktop playback was observed from the camera flow with simulated photo generation and from the calendar planner and cancellation controls. The camera UI smoke and phone dark-theme smoke passed. A camera companion unit test failed on Theo's availability. The broader convenience UI smoke stopped before the planner on its cancelled-generation state assertion.

releases.provenance: SFXMint's soft UI set was consulted. The four shipped effects reuse existing local arcade WAVs under the project's sign-in-free fallback.

releases.title: Browse your chess match history at the lounge
releases.summary: Look up your record against each chess opponent and inspect the captures from individual games.
releases.body:
In the Chess café Playing room, open Match history. Select an opponent to see every recorded game against them, newest first, with the in-game date and time, your result and the final move. Select a game to see how it ended and which pieces each side captured. Opponents remain listed when they leave the room. Practice and unfinished matches do not count.

Verification covered the in-person room button, a reloaded four-game series, a legacy match, selecting a second opponent, and both sides’ captures. The history screen was rendered and inspected.
releases.save_impact: Restart the game to open the new history screen. Existing recorded games appear automatically. Games played before match results were recorded are unavailable.
releases.provenance: Uses the existing story memory ledger. Verified with disposable story data and actual Tk selection events.

releases.title: Chess rematches and head-to-head records
releases.summary: Play another game from the result screen and ask an opponent about your overall chess record.
releases.body:
At the Chess café table, select Rematch after a win, loss or draw to start a fresh board against the same available opponent at the same level. The board displays your wins, losses and draws against that character. Direct conversations and texts with your opponent can refer to the full record as well as recent games. Only completed character matches count.

Verification covered three successive rematches, fresh boards and captures, independent opponent totals, a previous-format match memory, save/load and both direct conversation channels. The result screen was inspected.
releases.save_impact: Restart to load the changes. Existing recorded chess matches count automatically, and no migration is required.
releases.provenance: Verified using a disposable four-match series and the actual in-person and text prompt builders.

releases.title: Chess results, captured pieces and rematch conversations
releases.summary: See which pieces each side took and bring up the result the next time you talk to your opponent.
releases.body:
In person, visit the Chess café Playing room and choose Play chess. Both sides have a running tally by piece type, including en passant captures. A finished game displays You won, You lost or Draw, the reason, and the final move.

After a completed character match, ask the opponent about the game in person or by text. Both participants remember the outcome, finishing move and captures. Their recent shared games are available for direct callbacks. Practice and unfinished games do not create an opponent memory.

Verification covered win, loss, draw, captures by either side, en passant, a real Stockfish reply, saved-game reload, direct text and in-person conversation prompts, and isolation from a third character. The result screen was rendered and inspected.
releases.save_impact: Existing saves remain compatible. Newly completed character games are recorded from this update onward. Previous unrecorded games cannot be reconstructed.
releases.provenance: Checked with disposable story data, real save and load, and the actual conversation prompt builders. No live dialogue provider was called.

releases.title: Play chess against Winterfield characters
releases.summary: Challenge someone at the Chess café to a full game against local Stockfish, or take the practice board when the room is quiet.
releases.body:
Visit the Chess café and enter the Playing room in the in-person window. Open Play chess and choose a present opponent or level 3 practice. You play White. Select a piece to highlight legal destinations, then select its destination. The board supports castling, en passant and all four promotions. It displays check, checkmate and draws, and automatically accepts claimable draws. Leave table ends the session.

April, Sylvanis and the Crow share Stockfish skill level 20. Camila plays at 18 and Rei at 13. Other opponents play below Rei, using authored tiers or their established interests and traits. The Windows x64 engine runs locally.

Verification exercised the in-person room menu, the five named levels and remaining playable roster cap, illegal move rejection, a real Stockfish reply, knight promotion, a drawn ending and leaving during search.
releases.save_impact: Restart the game to load the board. Existing story saves need no migration. An unfinished board lasts only for the current table session.
releases.provenance: Implemented against existing room presence and character references. The smoke check used a disposable story and the bundled Stockfish 16 Windows x64 executable.

releases.title: Adult Rei campaign voice playback and replay
releases.summary: Adult Rei recordings now play with matching campaign dialogue, with replay, Voice and volume controls.
releases.body:
Added

In person → Story now automatically plays accepted adult Rei recordings when the matching dialogue appears in Rei’s and Garrett’s campaigns. All 280 recorded bindings are installed, including adult Golden Dragon memories and the selected RD31 acknowledgement. The two historical pilot lines use their first take; all originals remain preserved. Replay voice restarts the displayed recording. Voice and Volume controls use per-story reader preferences; existing master Sound mute also stops speech. Scene history permits manual replay without repeating story effects.

Compatibility and safeguards

Playback uses a dedicated local sound channel and never advances dialogue or commits an outcome. Navigation, leaving, loading, disabling and closing stop the clip. Redraws, scrolling and font changes do not replay it. A first-page saved dialogue resumes from the beginning of its recording when Voice is enabled. Captions remain available. Narration, other speakers, younger Rei, unrecorded callbacks, missing assets and mismatched legacy snapshots remain text-only. Exact words, source spans, conditions, viewpoint, era and file hashes guard against unrelated playback.

Windows playback

The accepted MP3 originals are unchanged. Verified 16-bit PCM/WAV fallbacks support Windows installations whose MCI MP3 driver fails. Per-clip volume scaling avoids changing global device volume. No online provider, account credential, extra speech generation or additional generation credits are needed during play.

Reusable framework

Other approved speakers can use the same accepted manifest, source resolver, controller and reader controls. The current catalogue/reflection adapters are shared; other source formats require explicit adapters and remain silent until supported.

Verification

89 relevant regressions passed with zero failures/errors/skips. All 280 installed MP3 hashes, 280 PCM hashes and 280 bit-exact decoded-audio comparisons passed. Five deliberately broken variants were caught. Real Windows MCI playback, replay, volume, mute/off, narration/unvoiced/navigation stops, no redraw repeats, read-only history, JSON resume and unmap passed. Five UI smoke scripts passed; normal, compact 24pt and disabled/history states were visually inspected. Final catalogue/test/export evidence is recorded in the integration plan.

Scope

This is the accepted adult Rei playback release, not full campaign voicing or a release of every MH-028 milestone. No further casting, generated audio, purchase or publication. Distribution entitlement remains unverified; ElevenLabs speech is not CC0.
releases.save_impact: Existing story text, progress, outcomes, flags and cursors remain compatible. Matching saved source segments can play; unmatched legacy text stays silent. Only optional reader Voice/volume preferences and source-bound presentation metadata are added. No save migration/reset. Restart a running game to load the changed Python code.

Tests, native Windows playback and rendered checks are actual execution evidence, with limitations and initial failures retained in the linked integration record.

Planning only

MH-028 records a shared voice roster followed by complete campaign production and in-person playback. Every authored spoken line will need campaign, scene, canonical speaker and era identity, individual delivery direction and an explicit one-output generation request. Scope and limits

The baseline contains 84 entries: 82 source-discovered entries and two historical-reference candidates, with 117 provisional variant/era records. Initial 82 raw labels and 4,104 structured occurrences are discovery evidence, not unique final generation jobs. Sixteen role labels and unstructured quoted speech still need reconciliation; full every-line direction is a later milestone. Child/teen provider capability, user-sourced Voice Design inputs, final casting and generation scope remain explicit gates. This plan does not expand the earlier four-line pilot credit exception. No new generation credits were spent, voices created, audio processed or runtime feature released.

Access

Read roadmap/CAMPAIGN_VOICE_PLAN.md, roadmap/campaign-voice/ROSTER.md and the detailed proposed creation prompts/source-era bindings in roster.json. There are no new game controls or campaign audio access instructions because playback is not implemented.

Verification

Full utterance attribution, listening, phone, game/save and runtime checks are not claimed.

The initial default-temp run stalled after one reported error and was interrupted; its incomplete log is preserved and its cause is not established. releases.title: Interpol: the men behind the case files
releases.summary: A fuller visual-novel campaign with longer scenes, distinct Fox/Gordon dialogue, Fox's mercenary past and three new illustrated recollections.
releases.body:
Changed

All 42 original Interpol sections have expanded prose, backstory, character thought and dialogue. Six objective openings and three substantial memories bring catalogue text from 10,551 to 20,760 words across all viewpoint and outcome variants. Thirteen cosmetic lead-order and confrontation-approach prompts have been removed from newly opened scenes; meaningful evidence, travel, attendance and combat requirements remain.

Fox is a pessimistic anti-hero prepared to kill anybody if he believes the greater good requires it. Gordon remains hopeful and committed to lawful, accountable action. Their disagreements develop through conversations and consequences. Fox's recollections establish his service in the Organisation alongside Kaden Mourne, Sylvanis and the conspirator who became the Crow, his survival of the coup, his continuing fight against the Syndicate and his grief for Kaden. No new compulsory killing or changed case ending is introduced. Dialogue uses character-specific written voices; this release adds no recorded voice acting.

Added

A mercenary-era Fox portrait with transparency, an Organisation infirmary background and a mourning-workshop background. Existing historical cast portraits and Interpol paintings remain in use. Fox owns these memories even when Gordon is hearing them; historical scenes do not place Gordon in the Organisation.

Access

Restart the game, load Fox or Gordon, and open In person → Story or Interpol. Continue the existing cases to read new scenes. Earned Revisit buttons let progressed saves read the three new recollections after the rail case, Crow trail and Night Ledger respectively. Meet the other protagonist in the Interpol briefing room without additional joined companions. Revisit grants no evidence, money or case progress. In-person activities stay in the in-person window.

Verification

100 tests across eleven focused suites passed, including both protagonists through all 24 Ace enquiry orders, saved-scene compatibility, earned replay guards, historical portraits, current fixed defeat and legacy capture. Three deliberately broken implementations were rejected by their intended assertions. Nine new rendered reader states, the existing Interpol UI smoke and the 34-page dark-phone smoke passed. Normal and compact/24pt views, real reader controls, scrolling, historical cast removal, Fox's memory ownership and the earned Story button were inspected. Detailed logs, art provenance, editorial review and final release-reader checks are linked from the delivery record.

Known limitations

Existing active and archived scenes retain their saved text. Newly opened scenes use the expansion; completed cases do not automatically replay. Existing startup warnings about five unavailable standard sound cues remain. This release does not claim a repository-wide regression pass or an independent external reader review.

releases.title: Takeo: Empire of One — expanded story and character depth
releases.summary: Longer visual-novel scenes, distinct dialogue and deeper Directive 0, Kazama, Onami and Shinokami history, with fewer administrative story steps.
releases.body:
Changed

Expanded all fourteen present-day chapters and all eight historical sequences. Comparable chapter briefing/aftermath and memory prose grows from 2,054 to 9,705 words, excluding the additional return/action pages. Scenes now develop setting, backstory, character conflict and Takeo’s mentality through sustained prose and dialogue.

Directive 0 shows the access and freedom Takeo valued, the human costs he dismissed, and his rejection of its ethical dissolution. Onami remains an organisation he chose to serve: he respects Shinzo Kazama’s absolute strength, world-conquering ambition and willingness to pursue power at any cost. The 2024 conquest and 2027 UN defeat remain distinct. Takeo subsequently founds Shinokami from the remnants to command the surviving force, retain the research and continue expanding power under his own authority. He does not become an Onami co-founder.

The research, One and Thirteen scenes establish his lack of empathy, willingness to experiment on his own son, social Darwinist convictions and treatment of people as instruments. His beliefs remain his own, not the narrator’s judgement of human worth. Kazama, Arakawa, Sylvanis, Thirteen, Keisuke and the historical supporting cast have distinct motives and speech patterns. Takeo’s tactical adaptation does not become a redemption arc.

Reading flow

Recollections now play through the in-person reader and return directly to the present with a scene-specific transition. The extra observation/context choice and separate return step are removed from new playthroughs. Nine non-choice command decisions commit after the relevant scene’s final page, without an additional report-confirmation action. The personnel/equipment choice still has its two material costs; combat, preservation and archive destruction still require their real objectives.

Access

Restart the game, select or load Takeo, and open In person → Stories, guards & gang properties → Story. Use Maps and the indicated rooms for travel. Start a new Takeo story to read the full expansion from the opening if your previous campaign is already complete. Scenes and historical activities remain in person; existing dark phone styling is retained.

Continuity

Fourteen chapter IDs, eight memory IDs, both transport consequences and the sole Empire of One ending are preserved. Pacific Relay and Thirteen’s command survive; Takeo personally destroys the unique contested archive, with no complete backup; Arakawa withdraws alive without it. The index is not a backup. No new Neo identity/address disclosure, reunion, named killer of Kazama or the other subjects, experimental mechanism, combat-stat change, art or audio is introduced.

Verification

65 focused/shared regressions pass, including eight new narrative-flow tests, saved-reader compatibility, privacy/arrival gates and real save checks. Both complete routes pass their gameplay assertions through 1,279 actual widget invocations, including five victories per route, memory/reader disk resume and equipment-route combat concede/retry. The initial personnel process encountered a test-harness cleanup error after completion; callback-owner cleanup was repaired and the equipment process exits successfully. Narrative, campaign UI and dark-theme smokes pass; expanded scenes were inspected at normal and compact 24-point sizes. All 34 phone pages pass the dark-surface audit. Story Skills maintenance passes for the represented editorial records.

Known verification limitations

Three unrelated shared-prose checks fail: a compiled/library mismatch and two Interpol FD39 errors. All three reproduce with pre-update Takeo modules. They are documented separately from the passing Takeo checks. Existing optional sound-load warnings remain outside this text update.

releases.title: Neo: A Life of His Own — expanded story and dialogue
releases.summary: Longer visual-novel scenes deepen Neo's reluctance, grief, survivor guilt, bond with Alyssa, hatred of Takeo and anger at Hachimura, with fewer generic progression clicks.
releases.body:
Changed

Rewritten all fourteen chapters and six memories with fuller scene-setting, interior narration and character-specific dialogue. Comparable chapter/memory/return text grows from 2,939 to 10,767 words, excluding additional choice scenes and private disclosures. Neo's ordinary life and refusal are established before the attack; Mariko's death, the continuing retrieval threat and living captives drive his decision to work with the rescue crew. He does not rejoin his father's organisation.

Mariko has more ordinary life, humour, disagreements and memories before her loss. Neo's grief continues through practical arrangements, interrupted habits and remembrance. His guilt about the dead subjects and leaving Thirteen remains emotionally real without proving that a ten-year-old could have saved everyone. The historical killer remains unknown. His hatred of Takeo concerns coercion, fatherhood and being valued only for performance. Empathy for Thirteen coexists with accountability for his current command.

Alyssa is developed as Neo's equal partner and anchor through shared work, humour, chosen closeness, disagreement and practical support. She retains her independent rescue work and boundaries. The Hachimura confrontation has sustained anger and aftermath: victory stops him without requiring forgiveness or making grief vanish. Named private listeners now have distinct replies to Neo's programme and parentage disclosures.

Story flow

New memories complete only after their final reader page, without two generic reflection selections and a separate completion button. Encounters start directly from Story after the authored scene. Tactical choices, real combat, travel, private meetings and the ten captive handoffs remain meaningful requirements. Post-combat outcome scenes precede the Hachimura/Thirteen decisions and are not repeated on continuation. Expanded spoken scenes require their actual listeners in the room.

Access

Restart, choose or load Neo, and open In person → Stories & organisations → Story. Start or continue A Life of His Own. Physical scenes remain in the in-person window; use Maps for earned travel destinations.

Continuity

Stable chapter, memory, choice, encounter and ending IDs remain. Mariko is the sole present-day death; Tyler's father survives with his existing disability. Hachimura and Thirteen survive in custody, Takeo remains at large, and Neo and Alyssa retain their home and partnership. No new artwork, audio generation, combat balance or automatic romance milestone is added.

Verification

60 focused route/reader tests pass, including 25 Neo campaign tests, full route progression, memory final-page completion, saved-reader and legacy-session resume, old post-combat choices, recipient privacy and actual listener presence. Neo Story/reader, phone dark-theme (34 pages), shared campaign presentation, patch-note UI and start UI (29 previews) checks pass. releases.title: Sylvanis: the Crazed Demon — expanded campaign
releases.summary: A substantially expanded visual-novel campaign with deeper Crow tension, Blisk origins, earned fear, unfulfilled supremacy, the Martos experiment and a new illustrated night-alley scene.
releases.body:
Added

Expanded all sixteen present-day chapter scenes and all ten fixed memories. Comparable chapter-opening and memory text grows from 2,359 to 10,257 words, excluding aftermaths, endings and duplicated presentation metadata. Sylvanis’s early crimes now include killings, destruction and destabilisation, showing how he became the Crazed Demon / Demon King and the most feared man on the planet. His Blisk origin explores a civilisation founded on dark magic, social Darwinism, violence and selfishness, and his contempt for its predictable ambitions. This does not make every Blisk individual alike.

The Crow knowingly uses Sylvanis’s reputation, intelligence and strength despite his volatility. Sylvanis uses the Crow’s ambitions as excuses and infrastructure for his own violence. Both manipulate one another without removing Sylvanis’s choice or responsibility. His supremacy supplies little lasting fulfilment; thrill, chaos and the possibility of a satisfying opponent drive the research. In the expanded Red/Blue memory, Sylvanis asks early-service Martos to fight a Red-enhanced subject. Martos decisively kills the subject, then notices a mild nosebleed. That narrow, unexpected result intrigues Sylvanis; it does not establish a near-victory or an equal.

New illustrated shot CS-SY08 shows early-era Sylvanis standing in a ravaged night alley among fallen attackers. It appears at the reputation memory’s aftermath and is also in his gallery. The original, exact prompt, reference snapshots and hashes are retained locally.

Changed

Routine roster, reservation, archive, programme and cancellation steps now settle after their authored scenes. Memories return directly to the story after the final page. Continuous in-person reading pauses for meaningful choices, actual fights, required travel, unavailable speakers or privacy restrictions. Older half-finished memory sessions offer one Continue the story control. The three provocation choices, real exhibition and four-exchange Crow finale retain their outcomes and costs.

Access

Restart, select or load Sylvanis, then open In person → Stories, guards & gang properties → Story → The Crow’s Patience. Continue at the required room and arrange actual participant arrival where needed. Scenes remain in person. Maps travel and room/privacy gates remain real requirements.

Continuity

Kaden’s genuine goodwill and question before death, the conspirator’s concealed identity and implied-only parentage, Charles’s cover and independent sealed evidence, Garrett’s separate investigation, Takeo’s headquarters meetings and separate territorial story, and both arena shutdown outcomes remain intact. There is no redemption arc, new permanent Awakening or combat-stat rebalance.

Verification

Actual Tk campaign screens pass at normal/compact sizes and 24-point text; alley and Martos scenes were visually inspected. Phone dark-theme smoke passes across 34 pages; player Story, twelve start-screen layout cases and patch-note UI smoke pass. Story Skills check and prose lint report no errors or warnings in the represented scope; that does not certify unrepresented game canon. Present scenes give Inez, Mara and Ansel room to challenge her. Separate specialist conversations distinguish Mavis's attention to handovers, Martos's concern for people and exits, and Elias's theatrical sense of timing. Both aftermaths include professional accountability, private father/daughter discussion, care from Mara and ordinary competitive enjoyment.

New memories return to the present after reading without two compulsory recap choices, removing sixteen filler clicks from a fresh route. Optional historical activities and journals remain optional. The consequential evidence, cooperation, disclosure, combat and allocation actions remain playable. Both choices retain their actual costs, lost shifts and 40/15 reserves. releases.title: Garrett: the brother behind the bravado
releases.summary: Longer visual-novel scenes explore Garrett's grief, swagger, school years and bond with Charles, with a new symbolic leadership handoff and emotional family catharsis.
releases.body:

All 43 Garrett scene sections now contain expanded authored prose and dialogue. The complete conditional catalogue grows from 11,011 to 19,875 words: 8,864 added words across all variants, not a single playthrough. Everyday memories of his parents deepen their absence without inventing a death chronology or revealing their killer. His teenage school-crew violence, enjoyment of his reputation, protective instincts, private insecurity and adult flirting receive more space. Rei raises the possibility that Charles did not survive; Garrett refuses to abandon him.

Charles's protective burden-taking and Garrett's admiration for the strongest Red Dragon continue through the reunion and later protection chapters. In the late private brother visit, Charles settles Garrett's own coat over his shoulders, steps back and acknowledges him as the Red Dragons' leader. He tells Garrett their parents would be proud. The gesture is personal recognition, not an inventory reward or a promotion earned by beating Charles; neither reconciliation choice forces forgiveness.

Changed

Seven early quest-choice pairs now express conversational intentions instead of bookkeeping. Newly assembled GD07 scenes omit the redundant journaling reflection. Meaningful choices, documentary verification, retries, actual required victories, private disclosure and existing endings retain their effects. The conflicting fruit-shop backstory and its derivative reference passages now follow the established school confrontation at Garrett sixteen and Charles twenty-one; Charles remains responsible for his violence.

The mantle scene is in the later A brother, not a weapon chapter, after the protection missions. Use a new Garrett story or a save before the relevant scenes to read the whole expansion.

A current notice gives the investigation a clear starting point; the journal separates facts from fear instead of supplying repeated filler actions. Jun and Luis, adult Iron Circle acquaintances, disappear after Blackstone assessments. Independent referral, collection and authorisation evidence makes the investigation personal.

Marcus's death now provokes an immediate angry reaction that Emily and Sophie interrupt. Increasing sleeplessness, vigilance and fear culminate in Rei's breakdown at the Blackstone loading entrance and a heated executive confrontation. releases.body:

All physical scenes, historical visits and fighting stay in person. Sowon, Kouji Mitaka, Paul Samsen and Somchai are persistent residents and Ivan starts with their contacts; other protagonists can meet them normally. Existing saves receive additive residents/contact migration without resetting explicit contact choices, nicknames or relationships. No Grove account or new romance/protagonist is invented for them.

A Life on Loan has eighteen chapters, eight bounded historical accounts, local choices with callbacks, and one protected ending. Ivan defeats April, Garrett, Neo, Daniel and Tyler and deliberately spares them before Sylvanis arrives. He draws a little blood, loses and remains a captive Syndicate member, attempting restraint with friends’ support. The six linked tactical samples use actual resolver exchanges and explicit fixed-story outcomes; zero-exchange concession cancels without advancing. No escape, clean absolution, repeated grant or permanent Sylvanis injury is awarded.

Five seven-technique kits plus five shared channel/endurance states implement the generals’ forty planned entries. Blue movement, fire force/stability, ice reaction and local footing/barrier, red attack amplification and wind soul injury/endurance remain distinct and finite. Non-wind generals cannot activate Misanthropy; Somchai does not automatically agree to friendly sparring; restrained sparring suppresses soul injury. New general B baselines do not alter Ivan A+ or Sylvanis S+.

Artwork

Thirteen room/location paintings, five transparent main-style portraits including Ivan at eighteen, and nine illustrated shots in three sequences are installed. Four portrait sources are reused in ordinary combat. Portraits match the main cast’s head-to-mid-thigh crop and drawn manhwa style. Somchai has extensive tattoos including his face and a more deranged expression. Opaque operational masks stay concealed; the small blood mark is at Sylvanis’s glove seam. Originals, supplied identity references, exact prompts, hashes and superseded drafts are retained locally. Built-in image generation supplied the art; its exact model identity was not exposed.

Known historical boundary

Eight historical periods are registered in three collections. The independently referenced age-eighteen waiting interval has three connected rooms and harmless inspection/practice with exact present-state restoration. Seven periods with unspecified required ages/reference data remain deliberately locked under the user’s instruction. Birth/fetal material is archival, never playable infant memory. No ages or parent identities were invented to bypass the gate.

The focused shared-system subset passes 110 tests; the separately recorded full diagnostic run of 115 tests still has four failure records and one error in two existing suites: three Valentina attraction expectations, a Garrett faction-standing expectation and a restricted Glasshouse travel assumption. The full run is not claimed green. Four intentional negative controls were caught by assertions. Ninety-six seeded resolver samples completed without runtime errors; they are descriptive, not guaranteed matchup outcomes. Actual Tk Story/reader normal and compact states, 24pt text, all portraits/shots, historical rooms, dark contacts/threads and four combat profiles were rendered. The 34-page dark-phone smoke passes. Live provider-generated dialogue and a human beta read were not performed. Existing sound-load warnings remain; no new audio is included.

Select or load Sylvanis, then open In person → Stories, guards & gang properties → Story → The Crow’s Patience. Follow actual room objectives through Maps and arrange the required appointments. Sixteen chapters and ten mandatory histories cover wartime arrival, immediate criminality/mastery/fear, the genuinely protective Organisation and Kaden Mourne, the open conspiracy and coup, expansion, live trials, the eastern murders, Charles’s admission and the first Takeo supply agreement. Kaden asks his required question while alive. Sylvanis willingly chooses evil for amusement and never redeems himself. The bespectacled conspirator’s face stays featureless; parentage is implied, never confirmed.

Before the Cards supplies six optional rooms in four unlocked periods with exact-era reference/voice pairs, ordinary activities, conversations and a separate journal. Recollections cannot change the live clock, inventory, relationships or other campaigns. A saved Crow custody outcome remains intact and makes the present route explicitly unavailable.

The exhibition and four-exchange ledger interception use actual combat. Spending real contested exchanges can retain the ledger while the separate arena shutdown proceeds. Exhibition success, physical performance and retained assets are recorded separately, including concession and a retained ledger after a failed display. Both endings close the arena, settle stock/records/equipment and the campaign operating account, then complete the HQ → Takeo HQ → Glasshouse aftermath. Charles’s bounded evidence success survives without completing revenge or disclosing anything to Garrett. The territorial betrayal remains unresolved.

Artwork and presentation

25 accepted paintings: eight transparent portraits, ten locations and seven core story paintings. All eight portraits were regenerated after the user corrected full-body framing; production now matches the main portraits’ head-to-upper-thigh crop. Superseded originals, exact prompts, reference snapshots and hashes are retained. The 138 authored shot elements use dialogue bubbles followed by separate prose pages, reusable staging and selected core paintings, with saved reading/room resumes.

Compatibility

The expanded shared run executes 233 test methods with seven failure records, zero errors/skips: four missing non-Sylvanis combat portraits, an outdated 24-versus-28 roster assertion, and two Glasshouse fixtures expecting privacy/empty NPCs where guards are present. The latter two also fail with Sylvanis hooks disabled. Existing tests were not weakened or skipped. Existing missing configured sound warnings, independent human manuscript review and live generated wording remain outside the certified result. Complete logs and review limits are linked in the release evidence.

releases.title: Martos: What He Holds
releases.summary: Play Martos’s complete fourteen-chapter story, eight memories and historical service years, with real protection, records and custody outcomes.
releases.body:
Added

Play as Martos, then open In person → Stories, guards & gang properties → Story. What He Holds follows his conventional and special-forces service, conscious participation in abusive orders, refusal and limited escape, recruitment by the Crow, costly care honoured, sustained Rage-control work and knowing service as Clubs. Fourteen chapters and eight required memories lead through the present protection of Lena Varo, an independent survivor whose account implicates him. She is separate from the existing archive-conservator character Lena.

Lena may reject protection terms and compare a viable revised arrangement without being teleported or failed. Her agreed recipient, route/fallback, records ownership and permitted disclosures are saved. Her unaltered account receives an authenticated receiving receipt. Present pursuit observations remain separate from historical testimony. The three-room transfer house uses normal Maps travel, doors and appointments; physical scene changes save the reading position and wait for actual room arrival. Sera’s voluntary private visits and each colleague’s scoped contribution are distinct from combat authority or forgiveness.

Real protection and outcomes

Present combat uses the ordinary engine, actual health/stamina/mana and knockout recovery. Paid approach costs and a route-local resource condition persist across retries and recover with ordinary elapsed time. The protected leg advances through resolved meaningful exchanges; utility recovery alone cannot deliver it. Reporting strain restores no resources. Handover needs recorded pressure, the control commitment and an agreed, available colleague. Unsupported overextension can lose a secondary sheltered route. Defeating Voss alone does not deliver Lena or the records.

Delivery requires completed protected departure, the intact original account and available authentication/cover colleagues in the receiving room. Securing Voss is separate: return to the defeated commander, disarm him, pay the perimeter costs with available cover and wait for the authorised custody receiver. The saved transfer records its predicates, receiver and time. Prioritising delivery over the secondary custody perimeter leaves Voss escaped and records the continuing risk. Full success and delivered-at-a-cost outcomes have complete Lena/Sera/Crow aftermath; withdrawal and recovery remains incomplete. The lounge watch repair has an actual appointed/private Mavis exchange or a solitude fallback. Neither safety nor custody grants conviction, forgiveness, redemption or a change to Martos’s loyalty.

Historical visits and artwork

Four required memories use fresh exact-era playable encounters. Conventional/selection kits do not borrow present titles, signatures or Path; later extraction uses bounded authored Rage reinforcement. Historical wins, losses, retries and abandonment leave the rest of the present save unchanged. Sera’s historical overmutation injury remains fixed history. Six optional service-years rooms span selection, later deployment, refuge and early service, with gated periods, exact historical voices, local journals, arranged Voss/Sera meetings and paused present time. Optional cooking, repairs and conversation grant no combat or campaign progress.

Thirty new paintings include fourteen transparent portraits, eleven locations and five source-bound core illustrations. Present HQ Aces and Sylvanis retain their existing masked Syndicate uniforms; neutral present combat and historical service/recruitment use their correct costumes, captions and portraits. Normal, compact and 24pt reading layouts, combat/retry and actual receiving/custody controls were rendered and inspected. Existing phone handoffs stay dark.

Compatibility and validation

A narrow legacy repair restores a missing professional Crow discovery only when a canonical professional starter already has his saved number. Explicit unknown records, outsiders, unrelated state and protected custody remain unchanged. It does not invent a new custody/number rule.

351 combined campaign/Mavis/Martos/combat/authority/interiors/save tests passed with zero failures, errors or skips. The final overlapping 21 Martos checks passed after scoped privacy/aftercare adjustments; they include full fourteen/eight supported and cost paths, actual full-health wins and natural historical defeat, saved branch outcomes, exact recipients, no-leak retries, forged-result rejection, all thirty asset hashes/portrait alpha and five core source anchors. Six existing UI baselines, the final Martos feature smoke and final phone-dark smoke passed. Patch-note validation/export and reader/start-screen checks accompany this release. Full evidence, fixed-seed balance limits, assistant-versus-human review scope and baseline missing-sound warnings are recorded in the linked release ledger.

releases.title: Mavis flashbacks: master moves and Mist skills
releases.summary: Historical Mavis can use supported master Silat moves and her existing Mist skills, including in an already-active saved fight.
releases.body:
Fixed

The age-twenty combat kit used by Mavis’s mandatory predecessor and provisional-service memories (MV-F02 and MV-F04) now meets the supported martial/Silat 80 threshold and includes four master Silat moves, six existing Mist unique skills and three existing Mist amplifications. The previous kit stopped at 72 and used a historical identifier that did not seed Mavis’s catalogue skills.

Masters include Serpent lattice, Phantom crescent, Falling canopy and Mirror snare. The existing Mist skills are Black-Vapour Slip, Hollow Counter, Veilbreaker Palm, Shrouded Sweep, Smokebreak Traverse and Midnight Curtain. Select them in the in-person fight’s Martial or Unique skills category; normal stamina, mana, targeting and combat rules still apply. At the historical kit’s refinement, the tested master costs 20 stamina, Mist unique costs 14 stamina/15 mana, and a Mist amplification on a basic martial move costs 7 mana. Skills can miss or be interrupted; availability is not a guaranteed hit or immunity.

Existing active fights

A versioned repair now adds the missing capabilities to an already-active matching historical player kit on load or idle encounter open/refresh. It preserves spent health, mana and stamina, opponent, seed, turn, arena, checkpoint, clock and completed exchange payloads. No free heal, encounter reroll or reward is applied. Existing learned entries and the legacy generic Mist amplification remain valid. Present Mavis, unrelated/custom profiles, completed history and the stronger prior Spade are unchanged.

Restart the application to load the changed code, then Continue your save or reopen the encounter. You do not need to lose the fight, restart the story or abandon the checkpoint to receive this repair. The historical kit keeps its existing identity, Mist, power, refinement, fight IQ and Path baseline; no present-day title or new power is copied.

Validation

80 focused gameplay checks passed, including exact kit contents, active/profile-only and idempotent repair, actual disk load/save, unchanged spent resources and opponent, pending resolved narration, paid engine actions and insufficient-resource rejection. Actual Resolve-button use and master/unique/amplification selections were rendered and inspected in normal and compact in-person windows. The full-health predecessor pilot was rerun on five fixed seeds with legal tactics, producing two genuine wins and three losses without injected HP or results. Exact evidence and existing sound-warning limits are recorded in the linked repair report.

releases.title: MH-004: Lived-In Interiors
releases.summary: Explore 539 distinct room views, meet people where they actually are, and continue existing stories with room-aware work, events, privacy and automatic outfits.
releases.body:
Added

Connected interiors across all 90 agreed building groups: homes, public workplaces, campus spaces, faction bases, headquarters, laboratories and custom properties. Every navigable view has its own finished image. Seven old primitive location backgrounds now resolve to finished illustrations. Garrett’s indoor living room and the archive’s outdoor forecourt have dedicated supplemental paintings; original finished artwork is preserved.

In person

Use In person after arriving, then follow adjacent door buttons. Room movement adds no story minutes. Knock at private doors, wait for occupied bathrooms, enter alone, reunite with waiting companions or invite someone present to continue together. Each companion needs their own clearance. NPCs use independent work, leisure and sleep rooms. Open zones share witnesses; people behind closed doors do not automatically hear, appear nearby or gain private knowledge. Amy and Minsu retain separate dorms with one public corridor.

Work, events and stories

All twelve JobSeek jobs and 32 protagonist careers/finales use authored work/review rooms, scoped staff access and actual temporary roles. Arrange shift, supervisor or career access in the in-person room controls, then walk to the named room. Existing deadlines, duration, pay and duplicate-reward protection remain. Calendar lets you choose an available room and dress context; arrive and join to attend. The phone plans and directs; physical activities stay in the main window.

Room-aware Charles, Rei, council, diplomacy, Bubblegram, Interpol and post-story protection flows preserve existing identities, branches, outcomes and private knowledge. New guard posts have separate stable IDs, while old victories and required mission rosters remain valid. The Crow’s scripted Interpol outcome is unchanged; owned properties gain no free guards.

Automatic appearance

Home, beach, actual training, formal and authored work contexts choose from each character’s available wardrobe. Leaving restores the saved baseline. Existing wardrobe controls support a visit-scoped manual choice and Automatic to resume. Required masks and uniforms retain priority, active scenes keep their appearance snapshot, and old photos/history are unchanged. No clothing is automatically bought or unlocked.

Access and saves

Restart the application, then Play or Continue. The complete catalogue is enabled atomically when play begins. Existing stories keep relationships, invitations, missions, ownership, guard wins, rewards and conversation history. No new story or reset is required. Damaged active references are blocked before migration commits, with the existing recovery path available. Unspecified dorm bathrooms remain non-interactive. Later campaign/artwork work remains paused.

Validation

236 targeted integration tests passed, covering all jobs/career work/finales, the complete Charles story, all three Rei endings, nine Interpol files and repeatable operations, original guard IDs, privacy/access, save migration, reservations, wardrobe and artwork. All 539 views rendered in the actual in-person shell with zero callback errors; all 27 render sheets were inspected. The 34-page phone dark-theme audit, required feature/compact-state smokes, patch-note reader and start screen passed. Source coverage records 794 classified stages and no unclassified consumer modules. The broader repository scan remains non-green; older source/lore/roster/local-romance failures and its source-snapshot comparison are detailed in the release evidence. No live-provider conversation evaluation is claimed.

releases.title: Neo's adoptive mother: proposed Mariko Ishida treatment
releases.summary: Develops a proposed mother identity, Interpol history and evolving bond across Neo's two home flashback periods. Editorial planning only; new details are not confirmed runtime canon.
releases.body:
Requested character development

The user asked to develop Neo's adoptive mother's name, personality, Interpol backstory and relationship with him, particularly across the two approved home periods. The recommendation is Mariko Ishida, replacing the earlier unconfirmed Naomi suggestion to distinguish her from the existing Naomi Sato. No existing resident, artwork or house is repurposed.

Proposed character

Mariko is sociable, brisk and affectionate, with choir rehearsals, radio dramas and a tendency to manage other people's problems too quickly when worried. Her proposed career separates field investigation and the established rescue from protected care, continued contact, independently reviewed placement and eventual adoption. A later move into support coordination and civilian community work gives her an independent purpose without unrestricted current records access. The new name, appearance, career details and name/adoption history remain proposals.

Two home periods

HOME-A develops Neo's willingness to express a preference or request without earning care through usefulness; proposed ordinary scenes involve an unfinished radio repair and leaving a light on. HOME-B allows humour and disagreement, including Mariko breaking an agreed check-in arrangement and taking responsibility for that overreach. Each period has distinct relationship and voice directions. Optional visits do not impose a recovery score, change historical deaths, resurrect her or leak adult knowledge. She remains non-playable and campaign-only, with the sole present-day death.

Editorial access and scope

Read writing/story-skills/characters/mariko-ishida.md and the linked Neo campaign plan. A bounded Neo reference supplies the reciprocal family relationship. The source map and roadmap distinguish these two editorial records from a full manuscript import or completed historical reference/style pairs. No runtime, scene manuscript, historical JSON, artwork or save changes are included; implementation order and existing pauses remain.

Verification

Story Skills character-management/scene-craft and Writer's Loop fiction-narrative informed the profile and era/source review. Installed Story CLI name checking, reindex, wordcount and check ran; the partial two-character workspace passes structural checks, with no chapter prose imported. Documentation/catalogue checks, patch-note unit results and export are recorded in the campaign plan after execution. No full-campaign continuity, gameplay or rendered-UI pass is claimed.

releases.title: MH-013 Stage 3: 146 wardrobe portraits prepared
releases.summary: Completed staged wardrobe artwork for ten characters, matching their installed Stage 2 masters and corrected heights; live installation remains pending.
releases.body:
Completed production

Prepared 146 transparent 1024x1536 wardrobe portraits: Amy 14, April 14, Emily 14, Garrett 16, Ivan 13, Minsu 16, Rei 17, Samantha 14, Sophie 14 and Yuriko 14. All final files were visually reviewed at full size and on whole-family, three-background and normal/compact runtime-loader sheets. The installed Stage 2 masters remain the identity/proportion references. The lower thighs, knees, lower legs and feet stay outside the frame; short hems reveal connected upper thighs, while full trousers, leggings and long dresses continue through the picture crop. The existing 70% visible-body fitting convention, shared scale and entire height registry are unchanged.

Corrections

Emily’s ivory formal outfit now has a continuous pleated skirt instead of a shorts-like split. Minsu’s charcoal pyjamas have both connected upper thighs below the shorts hems. Samantha’s affected swim/dress hands were rebuilt with complete visible fingers; her formal suit, red flannel and red motorcycle jacket also have continuous sleeves and complete hands. Yuriko’s pocketless outfits show complete hands. Additional repairs preserved April’s small pendant, Garrett’s exposed neck tattoos, Emily’s full gym leggings and clean alpha, Minsu’s original muted blue swim shorts, and Sophie’s picnic skirt length.

Authorized sleepwear change

The user approved covered sleepwear in original colours after image-tool rejections. Amy uses white, April black, Emily blush pink, Minsu charcoal, Rei charcoal, Samantha burgundy and Sophie cobalt blue. Garrett retains the original black shorts design; Yuriko has no separate sleep asset in this scope. Ivan’s original coral beach outfit succeeded on the identical retry requested by the user. The three failed attempts and their resolutions are recorded.

Access and provenance

Review roadmap/artwork-stage-03/candidates, README.md, manifest.json, reviews and screenshots. These candidates are outside live wardrobe discovery: the current game still loads existing wardrobe PNGs. This is a Development report, not an installed release. There are 167 successful built-in image_gen outputs including revisions; the tool does not expose its exact model identifier. Accepted files match raw generated PNGs byte-for-byte. Exact prompts, input roles, source/output paths and hashes are retained, alongside original snapshots and superseded candidates. No local pixel postprocessing was used.

Verification

All 146 final candidates pass format, alpha, margins, provenance and hash-bound visual acceptance. All 306 baseline live artwork/reference files and the complete corrected stature table remain unchanged. The staged audit passes 292 normal/compact height comparisons, 62 saved wardrobe JSON round trips and 26 automatic occasion/sleep routes. The real-loader smoke renders all 146 paths at two thumbnail sizes and captures 20 screens, including normal/compact in-person solo/groups and three dark-phone correction previews, with no callback errors. All were visually inspected. Its first run completed the gallery but failed on a nonexistent Ivan outfit in the scene fixture; the fixture was corrected and the full rerun passed, with both logs retained. Phone dark-theme smoke passes 34 pages and embedded controls; lifestyle smoke passes all eight apps and outfit-job states; start smoke passes 28 previews.

Known limits

Seventy of 71 tests pass across nine related unit suites. The existing camera test_local_date_partner_can_join_photo failure still reports Theo absent from its fixture. Tests are offline and do not write player saves or call AI providers. Historical, masked, combat and remaining guard artwork belong to Stage 4. Live wardrobe installation and complete-collection release remain pending; full MH-013 stays In progress. Catalogue validation passed with 498 entries, export refreshed, and the patch-note reader smoke passed. After correcting the preference test to select a default-visible entry instead of assuming the first entry is a release, five of six patch-note unit tests pass. The existing archive-source failure remains for missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg. Initial and corrected check logs are retained.

The 71 remaining Stage 2 display defaults now vary across 175-180 cm for male characters/roles and 160-165 cm for female characters/roles, rather than sharing 178/163 cm. All six integer values in each range are represented. Each identity has a stored value that remains stable across loading, resizing, navigation and saves. Explicit heights

Jeremy Gordon is 183 cm, Edward Fox 184 cm, the Crow 180 cm, Keisuke Hachimura 183 cm and Joseph Richter 190 cm. Oni and Custom Robotic are both 198 cm; these are explicit exceptions to fallback ranges. Richter's normal and cybernetic portrait paths, including the direct guard-art alias, resolve to 190 cm. Custom protagonists retain their own saved heights.

Access and presentation

Restart the game. Existing selection, in-person, prose, combat and phone portrait consumers read the revised shared metadata. The head-to-mid-thigh crop, 70% visible-body convention, uniform aspect-preserving fit, alpha-padding normalization and shared scene scale are retained. No missing lower legs are synthesized or stretched. No portrait PNG files were modified. Dialogue disclosure rules and gameplay attributes are unchanged.

Validation

The complete 107-master hash and paired-height audit passed at normal and compact sizes; all 199 non-master baseline assets remain unchanged. Twenty-nine targeted tests passed across framing, combat, guards and character selection, including exact original-record preservation, the seven overrides, varied ranges, reload stability, custom heights and aliases. The live UI smoke rendered all 107 paths at two thumbnail sizes and captured 41 screenshots without callback errors, including Fox/Gordon selection and both tall robotic roles at two window sizes. The first custom-robot smoke fixture incorrectly treated an image role ID as a built-in type; it was corrected to use a saved custom type, with both logs retained. Phone dark-theme smoke passed 34 pages and embedded controls; start smoke passed 28 previews. Updated galleries and robot combat were visually inspected. Publication checks are recorded with the follow-up evidence.

Scope

This refines Stage 2 rendering heights. The full artwork roadmap remains in progress; later wardrobe, historical and dedicated combat artwork production remains pending.

Publication checks

Catalogue validation passes with 488 entries, export is refreshed and the patch-note reader smoke passes. The patch-note unit suite has five passes and one pre-existing archive-source failure for missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg. All five changed Python files compile.

releases.title: Stage 2 portraits use consistent character heights
releases.summary: Install all 107 accepted default masters and correct relative stature, including Garrett and Rei beside Ivan.
releases.body:
Changed

Installed the accepted MH-013 Stage 2 default masters for 89 contemporary characters and 18 guard roles. One hundred runtime files are replaced; seven pilot masters are retained. All 107 installed PNGs match their accepted candidate hashes. Original files, before/after hashes and the complete height audit are preserved under roadmap/artwork-stage-02/height-review/. All 199 other portraits/reference files in the original baseline remain unchanged.

Fixed

Garrett (188 cm) and Rei (184 cm) previously looked much shorter than Ivan (193 cm) because the renderer mixed legacy/pilot sizing, included unequal transparent margins and gave the player a wider group slot. All 29 recorded heights are now retained through a shared stature registry. Missing male heights use 178 cm; missing female heights use 163 cm. Generic masked/robotic roles use a 178 cm display reference unless authored female. Defaults affect rendering only: concealed dossier facts, including the Crow's height, remain undisclosed. Custom characters retain their saved heights, including menu previews before live registration.

Portraits depict head to mid-thigh, with lower thighs, knees and feet off-image. Fitting models the visible crop as 70% of full stature, normalizes transparent padding and uniformly resizes both axes. It does not stretch anatomy or synthesize missing legs. Group scenes, prose compositions and combat pairs use the same pixels/cm for every participant regardless of slot width. The bottom is a picture crop rather than a foot position. Individual thumbnails reserve room for the tallest recorded master, 211 cm, so tall characters are not flattened to equal height. Character selection uses the same height data. Wardrobe previews keep RGBA transparency on the existing dark phone background.

Access

Restart the game and use character selection or the normal in-person conversation/combat routes. Default or Automatic portraits load at the existing filenames. Explicitly selected alternate outfits, headquarters uniforms, historical portraits and custom artwork retain their routing; select the default outfit to see a new contemporary master. In-person activities remain in the in-person window.

Validation

All 107 installed hashes, candidate hashes, backup hashes and paired stature ratios passed at normal and compact sizes; all 199 non-master baseline hashes remain unchanged. Stage 2 asset verification accepted 107/107, with zero pending. Seventy-three tests passed across nine relevant unit suites, including all-character ratios, individual tall thumbnails, saved custom height resolution, selection, guard/combat routing, hangouts, flashback saves and campaign prose. The installed-art smoke rendered all 107 paths at two sizes and captured 33 screens with no callback errors. Start-screen smoke covered 28 previews; combat smoke covered 24 dedicated portraits. Prose, flashback, patch-note reader and 34-page dark-phone smokes passed. Normal/compact groups, selection, all nine loader galleries, guard combat, historical scenes and dark wardrobe/control states were visually inspected. Publication checks are recorded in the follow-up evidence.

Known limitations

Full MH-013 remains in progress. Wardrobe, historical, masked and dedicated combat artwork production remain in later stages; their existing files were not regenerated here. Shared scaling cannot eliminate pose/effect differences or turn a legacy bust/waist composition into mid-thigh artwork. The 70% visible-body fraction is a staging convention, not a measured full-body reconstruction. Tests use fixtures/mocked providers and do not write player saves or call live AI services.

Patch-note validation and export pass (487 entries), and the reader smoke passes. The patch-note unit suite has five passes and one pre-existing archive-source failure for missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg; no historical evidence was fabricated to hide it.

Visit flashback area previously created a separate modal window. Location and hangout entry buttons now mount the historical scene in the main in-person content area. Reopening or refreshing an active visit reuses that view; loading an active visit restores it there. The phone stays hidden during visits. Return to the present restores the existing location or hangout; Escape closes the journal first, or returns from the visit. Companion selection, historical portraits/backgrounds, speaker paging, speech/actions, cancellation, error drafts and isolated memory history retain their existing behavior. Destroying or rebuilding a view cancels its polling and discards unfinished replies without ending the saved visit.

The dark in-person novel reader adds immediate text, 11–24 point type, previous/next pages, saved positions, required reflection choices, historical artwork, completed scene history and an earned-evidence recap. Authored reflection and recipient-specific disclosure records supply later continuity without relationship rewards or cross-campaign knowledge.

The five existing required memories now occur at their relevant story gates. Existing objective handlers still own evidence, travel, time costs, permissions, guard progress, fights and rewards. Access

Main-route context remains available when a visit is skipped. History never repeats an action or reward.

Validation

Nine campaign/reader/phone UI smokes passed; rendered large and compact scenes, historical/present returns, reflections, history and visit controls were inspected. The phone check covers 34 pages plus chat/contact/embedded controls. Known verification limits

The original external Fox/Gordon reference files remain unavailable; approved undated partnership history is explicitly an authored Winterfield adaptation. AI checks use mocked providers, not certification of live generated prose. The wider conversation-lore suite retains three previously reported character-data failures (29/32 pass). Five of six patch-note tests passed; historical archive-source coverage still fails on the pre-existing missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg. releases.title: MH-002 complete: creator writing, origins, identity and Trait kits
releases.summary: Finish the character-selection update with reviewed writing tools, portable profiles, private identities, complete starting origins and playable Trait-kit previews.
releases.body:
Added

Creator → Writing, identity & packages now provides explicit Expand/Rewrite/Format proposals, exact/fact locks, bookmarks, selective local randomisation, import/export with private-content controls, and isolated sample conversations. Proposals require review, preserve originals and reject stale results. Packages contain only a validated profile and transparent portrait; imported Trait approvals and signature acceptance are cleared.

Creator → Trait builder & practice adds structured prompts, resolver-backed kit/cost/interaction review, accepted-aspect specialisation, three role-guided signature candidates with one optional origin slot, old/new mechanics comparison, and disposable in-person practice. Awakened without a named Trait and latent-mana choices are supported. Starting signatures do not consume ordinary workshop cooldowns.

Starting choices now cover small-crew founders, returning professionals, narrative backgrounds, career interests, recognised credentials and prior portfolio. Shared balance supplies profession/branch contributions, strongest-history resolution and viable unawakened conditioning. Exact origin movebooks and stage clocks are seeded once.

Public/preferred names, aliases, familiar nicknames and explicit private disclosures use shared visibility rules in dialogue. Tools → Trait applications & identity disclosure opens in person. Supported aspects allow a bounded workplace check or public-surroundings survey with time/energy costs, presence checks, daily limits and repeat-action protection. No phone executes these physical activities.

Validation

192 relevant unit tests passed; creator-completion, character-selection, existing custom-creator, start-screen, expanded playable-cast and phone-dark-theme smokes passed. Inspected new dark pages, compact picker/creator, scaled keyboard focus, signature review and actual in-person practice/application renders. A 288-bout fixed-seed resolver matrix shows adjacent-tier growth and Exceptional Veteran below Rei in the representative comparisons. See roadmap/CHARACTER_SELECTION_COMPLETION.md for exact evidence and assumptions. Catalogue validation and Markdown export completed; patch-note reader smoke passed search, filters, reader state, export, error states and two sizes.

Known verification limits

AI responses are mocked in this pass; live provider output quality and latency are not certified. Semantic fact-lock review remains a player responsibility beyond explicit mechanical checks. Matchup evidence is a finite representative sample, not a universal win guarantee. Five patch-note tests passed; historical archive coverage still fails for the pre-existing missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg. No historical evidence was fabricated.
releases.save_impact: Restart required. Existing stories retain their saved progression, jobs, affiliations, learned moves and history; origins are not reapplied. Future stories from reusable profiles use the current starting balance. New optional profile/draft fields have legacy defaults. Imports create independent drafts; explicit library edits do not alter existing stories.

releases.summary: Continue MH-002 with six creator steps, a live profile/checklist, safe reusable-character editing, recovery comparison and selected-save previews. The Four Aces now list their Syndicate roles.
releases.body:
Added

After restarting, Create your own opens Identity & Appearance, Backstory, Combat, Career, Underworld and Review. Back/Next, direct step selection and Alt+Left/Right preserve inputs. Contextual help explains starting choices. Career and Underworld summaries use the shared origin resolver and open the existing starting-choice picker. Portrait and Live starting profile tabs remain reachable at compact size. Review shows the first field-validation problem plus portrait and Trait-acceptance requirements; full dossier remains available.

Select a custom roster character and choose Edit selected. Save character updates that reusable profile with its stable identity; Save as new character creates a separate profile, even for duplicate names. Appearance changes still require a matching portrait, and altered Traits require evaluation/acceptance. Story snapshots are never edited by this flow. A changed or removed source profile refuses stale overwrite and leaves the draft open.

Resume draft now previews manual and recovery copies, saved editor step, biography excerpt and changed sections. Stale draft autosaves/manual saves/pin updates are rejected by comparison with the last-read file. Save draft as copy preserves current inputs as a separate draft. These checks do not claim an operating-system-wide transaction lock across simultaneous processes.

Story library → Saved progress shows the selected JSON snapshot without loading gameplay or applying migrations. Saved combat/Path, funds, employment title and recorded reputation/heat come from that snapshot. Missing combat remains missing; starting funds and kit claims are omitted, and canonical occupation is labelled background information.

Fixed

Martos, Elias, Mavis and Camila now list Syndicate Ace of Clubs, Hearts, Spades and Diamonds respectively, alongside their public occupation records. They are direct specialists for the Cardmaster, not Suit commanders. Menu display does not reveal their roles to NPCs.

Validation

Eleven selection tests, two custom-library tests, eleven custom-protagonist tests and nine QOL tests passed. Selection, mocked custom creator, save-library, start-screen, phone dark-theme (34 pages plus controls) and patch-note reader smokes passed. Inspected compact live Review, staged Backstory, profile editing, recovery, Ace details and saved-progress screens; corrected compact clipping. Five patch-note tests passed; historical archive coverage still fails for missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg. No live AI was tested.

Remaining MH-002 work

AI writing/locks/ideas/randomisation, portable packages, disclosure-aware identity, remaining origins and balance calibration, advanced Traits and full end-to-end/accessibility coverage remain required. This entry records a delivered increment, not completion of MH-002.

releases.summary: All 28 canonical protagonists now have two-paragraph biographies and sourced personal details, including underground occupations. Creator history supports pinned revisions.
releases.body:
Added

Restart and select a protagonist, then open Backstory for two authored paragraphs grounded in the character references and story setup. Custom characters retain their own authored biography. Details now reads the original and expanded cast records: ages, occupations, calendar birthdays, heights and MBTI replace blanket placeholders. Garrett lists Golden Dragon ownership and Red Dragons triad leadership; Rei lists modelling/art and the Iron Circle underground championship; Ivan lists singing/modelling and his Syndicate executive role. MBTI is present for every canonical selection. Sylvanis (ENTP), Fox (ISTP) and Gordon (ISTJ) are explicitly labelled authored menu interpretations because their sources do not assign a type. Mavis remains Undisclosed for occupation; her birthday and those of Sylvanis, Fox and Gordon remain Unknown. Fox and Gordon heights remain Unspecified rather than invented.

Creator revision history now offers Pin / unpin selected revision. Pinned revisions survive beyond the latest 40 ordinary checkpoints. Unpinning makes ordinary retention apply on a subsequent save. Pinning preserves the working and recovery snapshots; failed writes retain prior data. Restoring the oldest ordinary revision now succeeds even when adding the pre-restore checkpoint causes retention to remove that revision.

releases.title: Guards keep their AI-generated replies
releases.summary: Fixes guard replies being silently replaced by the same greeting when the AI returns dialogue without narration.
releases.body:
Fixed

Guard conversations now accept an empty narration field when the AI supplies valid spoken dialogue. Previously, the common group validator rejected that response and the guard generator swallowed the error, saving a repeated stock greeting instead. This was reproduced live with Fox at Interpol HQ: the provider returned “Which files do you need?” while the game displayed the colleague greeting.

All conversation topics now use the configured AI provider, including the four suggested duty questions that previously used canned replies. The initial approach greeting and explicit guard-desk controls remain authored. Prompts include the player/guard names, recent exchange, duty guide, authority and desk facts, and instruct the guard to answer the latest line rather than repeat its greeting. Narration-free turns render as spoken dialogue without a fabricated narrator line.

Malformed or authority-contradicting replies receive one repair attempt. Persistent validation failures and provider errors reach the existing retry/error flow; they no longer commit a greeting disguised as an AI response. Valid command acknowledgements such as not needing clearance are no longer rejected by the overly broad phrase match. Guard command rules, contact restrictions and stale-result checks remain active.

Access and verification

Restart, continue the story and speak to a guard in person; existing guard conversations can continue. Sixteen guard-dialogue tests, six hangout-scene tests and three hangout-texting tests passed. The guard-dialogue UI smoke passed with a mocked narration-free provider reply through the actual asynchronous submission path; its compact conversation screenshot was inspected. Two live turns with the configured provider in an isolated fresh Fox state returned “Which files, Officer Fox?” and then a contextual response about requesting witness interview records through the records desk. The transcript is stored in tests/guard_dialogue_live_check.json. No player saves or credentials were changed. This small live sample verifies this reported failure path, not every possible generated response.

Release checks: catalogue validation/export, patch-note UI smoke and start-screen smoke (28 previews) passed. Five of six patch-note unit tests passed; the historical archive-source check still fails on missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg, unrelated to this dialogue change.

releases.title: Character dossiers, reusable profiles and creator drafts
releases.summary: Browse canonical and custom protagonists together, inspect starting profiles, save unfinished drafts and review initial career/combat origins. MH-002 remains in progress.
releases.body:
Added

The main menu now has full-name portrait tiles, name search, All / Canonical / My Characters filters, and Overview / Backstory / Details / Awakened dossiers. Compact windows place the dossier below the portrait. Selecting a tile never begins a story; Begin and Continue remain independent. Invalid library entries are reported and missing portraits do not remove reusable characters. Existing reusable profiles are recovered outside preview rendering, and duplicate names retain separate identities.

Open Create your own for Save draft, Resume draft, recovery copies, revision history, session Undo/Redo, optional public/private biography fields and Review. Save character returns to the selected roster entry without starting a story. Save & begin saves the reusable profile before using the protected story-start flow. Portrait generation and Trait evaluation remain explicit. Private history is visible in the owner's dossier and excluded from public biography; later disclosure routing is not yet implemented.

Choose career, criminal background & combat kit opens a dark Apply/Cancel picker. Twelve civilian careers expose their four supported starting titles, pay and hours. The current criminal choices cover clean/former/independent/freelance, trusted crew/lieutenant/captain, and faction member/specialist/field leader. Seven combat histories use the shared MH-001 scale, direct starting Path stages and explicit style/move selections. Recommended kits grant basics plus bounded advanced/master selections; unawakened builds cannot use superhuman masters. Employment and criminal standing initialise only for a new story, with prior experience separated from completed shifts and assignments.

Changed

Reusable profile identity is independent of subsequent edits. Saving an older playthrough cannot overwrite a newer reusable profile. Unreadable Continue data leaves recovery controls available. Emily's dossier reflects the active Critical Hit and Ascension defaults already present in current combat/lore code; there is no new progression reset or invented awakening history.

Known limitations / remaining MH-002 scope

This is an implemented foundation, not completion of MH-002. The full staged creator, richer authored biographies, published-profile editing UI, AI writing assistance/locks/ideas/randomisation, portable import/export, sample dialogue, full identity/disclosure routing, small-crew founder and returning-professional selectors, advanced Trait/signature/practice features and complete accessibility scenarios remain pending. Career combat contributions currently use small bounded tactical bonuses; profession-specific calibration and fixed-seed matchup evidence remain pending. B/low-A unawakened variants are explicitly labelled uncalibrated. Numeric targets do not promise victories. The saved-progress adapter exists but is not yet wired into the story-library viewer.

Validation

Seven new data tests, eleven custom protagonist tests, two custom library tests, 96 combat tests, 23 enhanced-combat tests, eleven job-app tests, twelve JobSeek tests and seven Bubblegram tests passed. New MH-002 UI smoke, existing start and custom-creator smokes, expanded playable-cast smoke and phone dark-theme smoke passed. The dark audit covered 34 phone pages and embedded controls. Wide/compact menu, creator, custom/empty rosters, Emily dossier, origin picker, revision history and Review were rendered and inspected. Providers were mocked; no live AI was tested. Patch-note unit tests: five passed, with the existing historical-source failure for missing tests/screenshots/mixtape-art-review-0.jpg retained. Full evidence and unfinished acceptance work are recorded in roadmap/CHARACTER_SELECTION_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

releases.title: Combat RPG interface: a larger arena and tactical command dock
releases.summary: Large combat portraits share the location backdrop, with RPG technique cards, readable HUDs and all eight approved MH-007 interface additions.
releases.body:
Changed

Restart and enter any fight through the existing in-person combat routes. Player and opponent portraits now occupy a shared location stage, with mirrored health, stamina and mana bars, objective and exchange phase, latest narration and a fixed resolve command. Moves and category buttons open scrollable technique cards; technique, amplification and target selectors remain directly available. Selection and inspection spend nothing. Forms / rules retains form activation, elemental channels, objectives, terrain, art filtering and concession. Completed encounters return to the location.

Added

Pin up to six learned moves and select them through Quick slots. History and Breakdown expose prior narration and recorded exchange outcomes; new UI-resolved exchanges also retain resource/state changes. Tactics toggles distance, terrain and partner information. Revealed bosses receive distinct framing and Richter's actual committed-action cycle labels. Gold hatching previews selected costs including form upkeep, not guaranteed damage or recovery. Click portraits or their name buttons for inspection; opponent techniques are limited to observed moves and operational titles respect knowledge. Display / help offers Detailed/Cinematic density, 10/12/14-point text and a dismissible/restorable first-fight guide.

Compatibility and limits

Combat remains in person and both fighters act within each exchange. No combat balance or animation assets changed. Smaller windows and larger text shorten secondary HUD labels; full names, states and technique explanations remain available in drawers. Older exchanges have no before/after snapshots and say so; their recorded costs and outcomes remain readable. Quick slots select actions rather than executing them. Existing resolve guards prevent repeated actions while narration is pending.

Verification

96 combat tests and 23 enhanced-combat tests passed. The new MH-007 Tk smoke covers layouts, preferences, keyboard card selection, saved active-fight restoration, unavailable moves, nonmutating selections, duplicate-submit suppression, provider fallback, depleted resources and missing art.
